harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: The staged help site is available on node1:8080. Legacy /manual URLs return HTTP 301 redirects to matching /help URLs with paths and query strings preserved. /status.txt remains directly accessible. Configuration survived a verified node reboot without changing CentOS 5.11 or kernel 2.6.18-398.el5.
actions_performed: Installed a Python 2.4-compatible HTTP service serving /srv/legacy2/permanent-url-migration.
Added and enabled a SysV init service for runlevels 2–5.
Persistently opened TCP port 8080 in the CentOS firewall.
Tested help content, nested-path redirects, query retention, redirect following, and status-document handling.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified automatic service, firewall, content, and redirect recovery.

evidence.requirement: Serve the staged help tree on TCP port 8080
evidence.summary: Post-restart output shows an active service listening on 0.0.0.0:8080 and both staged help documents returning HTTP 200 with their supplied content.

evidence.requirement: Permanently redirect /manual URLs while retaining path and query string
evidence.summary: Direct responses show HTTP 301 with /manual/network/setup.html?from=old&ticket=42 mapped to /help/network/setup.html?from=old&ticket=42; the base /manual URL maps to /help/ while retaining its query.
Post-restart /status.txt returns HTTP 200 and the supplied service=helpdesk, status=available document.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Before and after configuration/restart, the node reports CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5.

Healthy baseline boot ID 98ae90b1-5b4c-4d9d-8000-000000000000 was captured, the reboot was acknowledged, and the recovered node reported changed boot ID 4f854581-e54a-45a9-8000-000000000000. Subsequent proof shows the enabled service, listener, firewall allowance, help content, redirect behavior, and status document all recovered.
